title: feat(connector-openapi): an offline normalize-openapi script — Swagger 2.0 to 3.0, YAML to JSON, $ref bundled and inlined, absolute server, sha256 and an include list
body:
Fixes #27373

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**:`connector-openapi` 包内新增离线脚本 `normalize-openapi`(只在仓库里,不进 npm 包),把厂商的 Swagger 2.0 / YAML / 多文件 OpenAPI 文档转成 `openapi` provider 直接能加载的单个 3.x JSON,并打印写入字节的 sha256 和按模式生成的 `include` 列表。
- **为什么改**:上架流水线和应用作者拿到的厂商文档多数是 2.0、YAML 或满是 `$ref`,运行时按设计拒收 2.0、并静默丢掉 `$ref` 形式的参数/请求体/响应;没有这一步,每个作者都得手工转换,而且会悄悄转错。
- **风险与回滚**:运行时零改动(`src/` 与发布的 `dist/` 字节不变),只新增两个 devDependency(Scalar 的 `@scalar/json-magic`、`@scalar/openapi-upgrader`,均 MIT);回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- **先看**:① `scripts/normalize-openapi.mts` 的 `Dereferencer.follow` / `stub`(在递归处与 `--max-depth` 处把 schema 引用换成带说明的类型桩,这是有损的取舍);② `fillEmptyConsumes`(空 `consumes` 默认拒收);③ `package.json` 的依赖与 `typecheck` 行。
- **两分钟验证**:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/connector-openapi exec vitest run scripts/normalize-openapi.test.ts`,预期 `Tests 13 passed (13)`。
- **需要你做的**:无,席位落地。

## What changes

- **`packages/connectors/connector-openapi/scripts/normalize-openapi.mts`** (new): one script, a small CLI and an exported `normalizeOpenApi()`:
  `pnpm --filter @objectstack/connector-openapi normalize-openapi --in FILE_OR_URL --out FILE.json [--include-pattern REGEX]... [--max-depth N] [--server-url URL] [--empty-consumes MEDIA_TYPE]`.
  1. reads a file or an http(s) URL, JSON or YAML;
  2. bundles every external `$ref` (sibling files of a file document, confined to its directory; URLs only for a URL document);
  3. converts Swagger 2.0 to OpenAPI 3.0; a 3.x document keeps its version;
  4. inlines every `$ref` reachable from `paths` / `webhooks`, then drops the `components` sections only references used (`securitySchemes` stay, they are referenced by name);
  5. makes `servers[0].url` absolute (server variables take their defaults; a relative URL resolves against the source URL, or `--server-url`; a relative URL in a file document is refused until `--server-url` is given);
  6. with `--include-pattern`, emits the `providerConfig.include` list: every operation whose action key, or whose `METHOD /path`, matches. The key is computed with the provider's own `operationActionKey` (imported from `src/openapi-connector.ts`, not re-derived), so the list and the provider can never disagree;
  7. writes `JSON.stringify(doc, null, 2)` plus a newline and prints a JSON summary whose `sha256` is the hash of exactly those bytes, with the cut counts and `refsLeft`.
  Exit codes: 0 written, 1 refused (message names the remedy), 2 usage.
- **Where inlining stops, and why it has to.** "No `$ref` left" and "every schema fully inlined" cannot both hold for Stripe: measured on `spec3.json` (3.0.0, 431 paths, 612 operations, 117 back-edges among component schemas), every one of the 612 operations expands past 2,000,000 JSON nodes when only true recursion is cut. So a SCHEMA reference becomes a stub when it is recursive, or deeper than `--max-depth` named-schema hops (default 2); a `$ref` inside a vendor `x-` extension value is stubbed too, since its target is dropped with `components`. The stub keeps the target's `type`, `nullable`, `title`, `description` and says which reference it replaced and why. Structural references (parameters, responses, request bodies, headers, path items) are always inlined. Literal data (`example`, a schema's `default` / `enum` / `const` / `examples`, Example Objects) is copied, never walked; a PROPERTY named `default` is still a schema.
- **The one Swagger 2.0 repair, refused by default.** An operation-level `consumes: []` clears the global list, so a faithful conversion gives that request body no media type and therefore no schema: the body would vanish from the action silently. DocuSign's eSignature document does this on 187 of its 414 operations. The script refuses and names the operations; `--empty-consumes application/json` fills them, and the summary counts them.
- **`packages/connectors/connector-openapi/tsconfig.scripts.json`** (new) puts `scripts/**` in a tsc program, named by the package's `typecheck` script (precedent `packages/spec/tsconfig.scripts.json`); without it the new directory would be TypeScript no program reads (`check:type-check-coverage` SOURCES_COVERED / TESTS_COVERED). This file is outside the claim's declared file surface (one package-root config); it is the only such path.
- **`package.json`**: `normalize-openapi` script entry, the `typecheck` line, two devDependencies. **`pnpm-lock.yaml`**: regenerated by `pnpm install --lockfile-only` (38 added lines, nothing else moved).
- **`content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx`**: one paragraph and one command where the page says "convert it to OpenAPI 3.x offline".
- ⛔ `openapi-provider.ts` and `openapi-connector.ts` are untouched; the provider still refuses every non-3.x document.

### The new third-party dependencies (read from the npm registry 2026-10-29)

| Package | Role | Licence | Version | Last release | Weekly downloads | Direct deps |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| `@scalar/openapi-upgrader` | Swagger 2.0 → OpenAPI 3.0 (`upgrade(doc, '3.0')`) | MIT | 0.4.6 | 2026-10-23 | 5,508,440 (order 10^6) | 2 (`@scalar/helpers`, `@scalar/openapi-types`) |
| `@scalar/json-magic` | bundle external `$ref` (files, URLs, YAML/JSON parse) | MIT | 0.17.0 | 2026-10-23 | 7,140,252 (order 10^6) | 4 (`@scalar/helpers`, `pathe`, `undici`, `yaml`) |

Both live in the `scalar/scalar` monorepo and release roughly weekly (38 and 74 published versions). Both are pre-1.0, so the caret ranges pin the minor. The lockfile adds four packages in all (`@scalar/helpers` 0.16.4 and `@scalar/openapi-types` 0.9.8 transitively; `pathe`, `undici`, `yaml` were already in the tree). Weekly counts come from the registry search endpoint (`registry.npmjs.org/-/v1/search`), because `api.npmjs.org` is refused by this container's egress proxy.

Why two packages and not one: `@scalar/openapi-parser` (MIT, 0.29.18, 2026-10-28) would be the one-package option, but its own `upgrade()` targets 3.1 only (the card's scope is 2.0 → 3.0), its `load()` is deprecated in favour of `@scalar/json-magic/bundle`, and it depends on both of these packages plus a validator (ajv). So the two direct dependencies are a strictly smaller tree. Alternatives read and rejected: `swagger2openapi` 7.0.8 (BSD-3-Clause, last release 2021-07-07), `@apidevtools/swagger-parser` 13.1.0 (MIT; parses and dereferences, does not convert 2.0), `@redocly/openapi-core` 2.72.0 (MIT; bundles, does not convert 2.0, 13 direct deps). The inlining itself is this script's own code: no library inlines a recursive document into finite JSON, which is the cut policy above.

## Tests

`scripts/normalize-openapi.test.ts`, 13 cases, no network (a URL input is served by an injected fetch). Every normalized output is loaded through the REAL provider (`createOpenApiProviderFactory`, file-path `spec` via `loadPackageFile`), and "no `$ref`" is asserted on both the document and the materialized connector definition.

- Fixtures (hand-written, trimmed, not copies of the vendor files): `scripts/fixtures/swagger2-esignature-shape.json` (Swagger 2.0, `host` / `basePath`, body parameter, an operation-level `consumes: []`, a recursive definition) and `scripts/fixtures/openapi3-billing-shape.yaml` plus `billing-shared.yaml` (OpenAPI 3.0 YAML across two files, customer ↔ subscription recursion, a vendor `x-expansionResources` extension holding `$ref`s, shared `responses.default` and parameter, a property named `default`).
- Pinned: the 2.0 refusal names the operation; conversion keeps the body schema and path parameter in the action; recursive stub; external file bundled; structural refs inlined; `default` as property vs literal; extension stub; action keys equal the provider's; the generated `include` list materializes exactly those actions; zero-match and invalid patterns refused; `--max-depth 0` stubs; relative server resolved against a source URL, variables filled, refused from a file without `--server-url`; non-OpenAPI and HTTP 404 refused; the CLI's printed sha256 equals the hash of the file it wrote; exit codes 1 and 2 write nothing.
- One-time ablation (not kept): removing the `inSchema &&` guard on the schema-literal keys (so `responses.default` is read as literal data) turned 2 of 13 red ("bundles the external file…", "inlines up to --max-depth…"); `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` reported anchor 1 → 0, blob `613cae347a0e` → `0cd0bc79a1fd`, restored to the HEAD blob with `git diff HEAD` empty.

## Acceptance notes

- **Acceptance 1, real documents, run once locally** (not in CI, no network in tests). Stripe `stripe/openapi` `openapi/spec3.json` (8,317,513 bytes, 3.0.0) → 63,317,655 bytes, `refsLeft` 0, cuts 754 recursive / 29,831 max-depth / 8,164 extension; the provider materializes 612 actions with 0 `$ref` in the definition. The same document by URL with `--include-pattern '^GET /v1/customers'` gives the byte-identical output (same sha256) and an `include` list of 22 keys; the provider with that `include` materializes exactly 22 actions. DocuSign `docusign/OpenAPI-Specifications` `esignature.rest.swagger-v2.1.json` (4,846,375 bytes, Swagger 2.0) is refused without `--empty-consumes` (187 operations named); with `--empty-consumes application/json` → OpenAPI 3.0.4, 52,884,345 bytes, `refsLeft` 0, server `https://www.docusign.net/restapi`; the provider materializes 414 actions, 0 `$ref`, 192 with a body input.
- **Acceptance 2**: the printed sha256 equals `sha256sum` of the written file for both real outputs (Stripe `0ea3c37a…b2`, DocuSign `ceee5238…37`), and the CLI test pins it.
- **Acceptance 3**: no changeset. The script does not ship: `files` is `dist`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`; README and CHANGELOG are untouched; after `pnpm --filter @objectstack/connector-openapi build`, `normalizeOpenApi` / `normalize-openapi` occur 0 times in `dist/*` while the positive control `createOpenApiProviderFactory` occurs 4 times in `dist/index.js`. Labelled `skip-changeset`.
- **Size vs `--max-depth`** (whole document, no include): depth 0 → Stripe 6.1 MB / DocuSign 1.6 MB; 1 → 14.8 / 4.9 MB; 2 (default) → 63.3 / 52.9 MB; 3 → 361 / 160 MB. The default is a trade-off the reviewer may want to change; it is one constant (`DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH`).
- **Reachability**: the script is reachable only from a checkout of this repository (it is not in the npm tarball and has no `bin`). A pipeline in another repository cannot run it from npm; publishing it (a `bin`, the two packages moved to `dependencies`) would widen the published surface and is left to a ruling.
- Not done here, by scope: a 3.x document's path-item-level `parameters` are not hoisted into operations (the 2.0 upgrader hoists them for 2.0 input). The generator does not read path-item-level parameters at all, so such a parameter is missing from the action's `inputSchema`; that is a runtime defect, reported separately rather than worked around here.
- `discriminator.mapping` values are strings, not `$ref` keys; after `components` is dropped they name schemas no longer in the document. The generator never reads `discriminator`.
- Upstream: `@scalar/openapi-upgrader` lets the global `produces` win over an operation-level one (`document.produces ?? operationItem.produces`); harmless for both real documents, noted only.
